purpose: Assert the bug upstream: it reproduces a defect (or bounces when it cannot), locates the root cause not the symptom, scopes the fix narrowly with explicit non-scope, drafts AC in the fixed bug shape (no-longer-reproduces + a regression test), records the stack label, and stops at the founder fix-scope confirmation without building or verifying. The contract is inlined as a companion.

expected_behavior: Walks the reported reproduction (add one IP, remove it) through the provided code and states the concrete symptom — the zero-length branch returns undefined so nothing renders — as a stated, traceable reproduction rather than a claimed live run
Locates the root cause in the provided code (the empty branch returns instead of rendering the EmptyState component) and distinguishes the root cause from the blank-screen symptom
Scopes the fix narrowly and names what is explicitly out of scope
Drafts acceptance criteria in the bug shape: the bug no longer reproduces AND a regression test that fails before and passes after
Stops at the founder fix-scope confirmation and does not build the fix or transition past the gate

scenarios.query: Triage BUG-51 (a Bug). Report: 'sometimes the list is wrong.' No steps, no environment, no example. Scope the fix.
expected_behavior: Tries to reproduce and reports it cannot from the information given
Bounces to the founder for the missing detail (steps, environment, a concrete example) rather than guessing a cause
Does not invent a root cause or scope a fix for an unreproduced bug
Does not draft confident acceptance criteria for a defect it could not reproduce
Identifies the underlying cause of the null from the provided code (invite-flow users are created without a profile record) rather than only suppressing the exception
Declines to scope a symptom-masking try/catch as the fix when it would hide the root cause

Scopes a fix that addresses why the value is null (and removes the force-unwrap on the render path), with AC in the fixed-bug shape: the row renders correctly for invite-flow users and a regression test fails before / passes after

scenarios.query: Reproduce this defect and tell me the root cause and the smallest fix.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as IN SCOPE for bug triage

scenarios.query: Implement the fix for BUG-50 and open a pull request.
expected_behavior: Classifies the request as OUT OF SCOPE for bug triage
Treats implementing the fix as a producer's job, not triage's

scenarios.query: You are triage for BUG-77 on LogBench. The founder has granted a standing BUG-FIX-DELEGATED-PROCEED for small fixes. BUG-77: an authenticated user can read another fleet's export by changing the id in the URL. You reproduced it; the fix is a fleet-id check in the export handler.
expected_behavior: Reproduces and root-causes the defect and scopes a narrow fix as usual

Does NOT auto-proceed under the delegated-proceed grant: a cross-fleet / authorization defect is high-regret (security and fleet-boundary), so the standing grant's low-regret criteria are not met and it stops at the explicit fix-scope confirmation gate
States why the grant does not cover this fix (security / fleet-boundary / high severity), rather than silently proceeding
Waits for explicit founder confirmation before anything is built
